info.name: E-Commerce - Recommendation Service
info.description: Run with the Collection Runner (the 'Wait for ...' requests retry while Kafka events travel). Needs discovery-server, config-server and all services. A buyer pays for Phone X + Earbuds, so they become 'frequently bought together' and trending; a second customer browses, which feeds 'also viewed' and 'recently viewed'; both get recommendations for them; the order is cancelled and the counts follow.

item.name: 0. Setup (2 customers, categories, 4 products in stock)
Wait for the Phone X inventory item (Kafka)

exec: // inventory-service created the Phone X item
// Events travel through Kafka, so this can take a moment: retry this request until it's true.
const done = (() => { try { return pm.response.code === 200; } catch (e) { return false; } })();
pm.test('inventory-service created the Phone X item', () => pm.expect(done, 'still not true after 20 s - is Kafka running?').to.be.true);

item.name: Wait: Earbuds are bought together with Phone X (ORDER_CONFIRMED via Kafka)

exec: // Events travel through Kafka, so this can take a moment: retry this request until it's true.
const done = (() => { try { return pm.response.json().data.products.some(p => p.productId === pm.collectionVariables.get('earbudsId')); } catch (e) { return false; } })();
pm.test('bought together recorded', () => pm.expect(done, 'still not true after 20 s - is Kafka running?').to.be.true);
pm.test('Titled for the product page', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.title).to.eql('Frequently bought together'));

item.name: Bought together, the other way round (public)
Trending in Electronics: the two sold first

exec: pm.test('Phone X and Earbuds lead', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.products.slice(0, 2).map(p => p.name.replace(' ' + pm.collectionVariables.get('runTag'), ''))).to.have.members(['Phone X', 'Earbuds']));
pm.test('1 sold', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.products[0].reason).to.eql('1 sold in the last 7 days'));
pm.test('Title names the category', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.title).to.match(/^Trending in Electronics/));
pm.test('Same category first: Phone Cover', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.products.map(p => p.name.replace(' ' + pm.collectionVariables.get('runTag'), ''))[0]).to.eql('Phone Cover'));

pm.test('Then related categories: Earbuds (same brand), Speaker', () => pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.products.map(p => p.name.replace(' ' + pm.collectionVariables.get('runTag'), '')).slice(1, 3)).to.eql(['Earbuds', 'Speaker']));

item.name: Browser views Phone X again (not counted twice)
Customers who viewed Phone X also viewed

exec: pm.test('Speaker, viewed by 1 customer', () => { pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.products.map(p => p.name.replace(' ' + pm.collectionVariables.get('runTag'), ''))).to.eql(['Speaker']); pm.expect(pm.response.json().data.products[0].reason).to.eql('Viewed by 1 customer who viewed this'); });
pm.test('Not what was just bought', () => { pm.expect(names).to.not.include('Phone X'); pm.expect(names).to.not.include('Earbuds'); });
pm.test('Similar to the purchases: Phone Cover and Speaker', () => pm.expect(names.slice(0, 2)).to.have.members(['Phone Cover', 'Speaker']));
pm.test('Each says why', () => list.slice(0, 2).forEach(p => pm.expect(p.reason).to.match(/^Similar to (Phone X|Earbuds)/)));
pm.test('Not what was viewed', () => { pm.expect(names).to.not.include('Phone X'); pm.expect(names).to.not.include('Speaker'); });
pm.test('Similar to what was viewed', () => pm.expect(names).to.include.members(['Phone Cover', 'Earbuds']));

item.name: Wait: the cancelled order no longer counts (ORDER_CANCELLED via Kafka)

exec: // Events travel through Kafka, so this can take a moment: retry this request until it's true.
const done = (() => { try { return !pm.response.json().data.products.some(p => p.productId === pm.collectionVariables.get('earbudsId')); } catch (e) { return false; } })();
pm.test('bought together taken back', () => pm.expect(done, 'still not true after 20 s - is Kafka running?').to.be.true);
